questions.prompt: When writing alt text for an image, what should you avoid doing?
choices: Starting the description with "Image of..."
Describing what the image shows
Explaining why the image is there
Keeping the description concise

questions.prompt: How do you tell a screen reader to skip a purely decorative image, like a border or divider line?
choices: Check "Mark as decorative" in the alt text panel
Delete the image from the document
Leave its alt text blank
Type "decorative image" as the alt text

questions.prompt: Which of these should you use to create document structure in Word?
choices: All caps text
Built-in Heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2, etc.)
Bold and larger font size
Extra blank lines between sections

questions.prompt: What's the correct way to order heading levels in a document?
choices: Use the Title style for the main heading
Order doesn't matter, as long as every heading uses a Heading style
Start with Heading 1 for the title, then Heading 2, then Heading 3, in sequential order
Skip levels for a cleaner look, e.g. Heading 1 straight to Heading 3

questions.prompt: Why does a screen reader struggle with a list made by typing "*" or "-" in front of each line?
choices: It reads all the lines together as one run-on sentence, with no separation between items
It skips those lines entirely, as if they weren't there
It reads the character as text and never announces it as a list
It stops reading partway through the list, as if it hit an error

questions.prompt: What should tables in a Word document be used for?
choices: Data only, never for page layout
Mostly for data, but occasional layout use is fine if it's simpler
Either data or layout, whichever looks better
Laying out content visually on the page

questions.prompt: How do you tell a screen reader which row or column in a table contains headers?
choices: Bold the header text
Merge the header cells together
Check Header Row and/or First Column in Table Design
It's automatic - no action needed

questions.prompt: What's the problem with pressing Enter multiple times to add space between paragraphs?
choices: A screen reader announces each empty line as "blank"
There's no real problem with this approach
It causes inconsistent spacing when the document is viewed on different screen sizes
It makes the document print incorrectly

questions.prompt: Why is placing "First Name" and "Last Name" side by side with an invisible table a problem for accessibility?
choices: It looks unprofessional
A screen reader announces it as a table and forces cell-by-cell navigation instead of a simple form
It's only a problem if the form gets printed, not when it's filled out on a computer
It makes the document take longer to load in Word

questions.prompt: Why is light gray text on a white background a problem?
choices: It can make the document look less formal or polished
It's only an issue when the document is printed in black and white
It's a minor issue that only affects a small number of readers
People with low vision or color blindness may not be able to read it

questions.prompt: What's the correct way to mark a task as urgent in a document?
choices: Make the font larger
Color the text red AND add a word or symbol like "(Urgent)"
Add a colored dot with no label
Color the text red

questions.prompt: What's wrong with a hyperlink that just says "Click Here"?
choices: Nothing - it's a perfectly fine way to label a link
It isn't blue and underlined
It doesn't tell someone browsing a list of links out of context where the link actually goes
It's fine as long as the surrounding sentence gives context

questions.prompt: Why does setting the correct proofing language matter for accessibility?
choices: It only affects the spell checker
A screen reader applies the wrong pronunciation rules if it's set incorrectly
It only matters if the document will be translated into another language
It's only a cosmetic setting with no real effect

questions.prompt: Which text alignment should be avoided for readability?
choices: 12pt or larger font
Left-aligned
1.5 or higher line spacing
Justified (even left and right edges)

questions.prompt: What can Word's built-in Accessibility Checker NOT do?
choices: Flag low color contrast
Flag missing alt text
Flag a table that's missing defined headers
Judge whether your alt text is actually meaningful

questions.prompt: What's the correct way to export an accessible Word document to PDF?
choices: Export each page as an image, then combine the images into a PDF
Copy and paste the text into a PDF editor
Print to PDF
Use Save As/Export with the accessibility tagging options enabled

questions.prompt: What's the correct alt text format for a well-known logo, like your own organization's?
choices: "Logo: [Company Name]" - for example, "Logo: Benetech"
Leave the alt text blank since the logo is already familiar
A long, detailed description of the logo's colors and shapes
Mark it as decorative

questions.prompt: What should you do with placeholder text like "[Type your answer here]" left inside a form field?
choices: Leave it in place so people know what to do
Delete it - real content or blank space should remain, not bracketed instructions
Make it bold so it stands out
Replace it with a longer, more detailed instruction instead

questions.prompt: What's the minimum font size you should use for body text?
choices: 8pt
10pt
12pt (16-18pt is even better for low vision)
11pt, since that's Word's own default font size

questions.prompt: How should a hyperlink be visually styled?
choices: Plain black text, same as the rest of the document
Bold, but the same color as the surrounding text
Italicized
Blue text, underlined

questions.prompt: How should an email address be formatted in a document so someone can act on it right away?
choices: As a live, clickable mailto: link
As plain text
As an image of the email address
Spelled out with "(at)" and "(dot)" to avoid spam

questions.prompt: What should you do with Word's built-in Accessibility Checker before sharing a document?
choices: Nothing - it's purely informational
Run it and resolve the errors and warnings it reports
Run it once at the very start, before making any edits
Run it, but only act on the errors, not the warnings
